response: In Uttar Pradesh, activists are attacking the government for failing to set up any workable process for brick kiln operators to obtain environmental clearances, even three months after the mandate was supposed to take effect. This is the usual pattern with these groups, who use environmental rules as a weapon to harass traditional Indian industries and the workers who rely on them for honest livelihoods. The brick kiln owners already hold State Pollution Control Board approvals for water and air standards and have made clear they are ready to comply once the system is cleaned up and freed from middlemen interference rooted in corruption. What we need is for the state to exercise real authority, cut through the bureaucracy with decisive action, and enable these businesses to operate responsibly instead of giving in to activist pressure and legal experts pushing court decisions that only add more obstacles to our economic strength and cultural way of life.
